catalog_quote: It may also be observed that the short vowels do not occur in open syllables except when they are unstressed. ... There are six tones in normally stressed syllables, and only two registers for the unstressed syllables. ... Some proclitic and enclitic syllables are unstressed, and sometimes with vocalic modification of the stressed forms, if the stressed forms can be elicited. The unstressed syllables may have a high register or a low register. The high register is marked by a raised dot, the low register will not be marked. Thus, /kjaa 35/ is a prefix or a numeral classifier used with many objects, utensils, and some body parts, and is often unstressed to /kja˙/. ... The prefix /ne/ (low register) is often used with names of animals, but the stressed form is not known. new_statements.rule_in_words: T'en is a six-tone language in which every full lexical syllable is stressed and carries one of six tones; proclitic and enclitic syllables (noun prefixes/classifiers such as kjaa- > kja', ne-, the numeral te' 'one', pronouns) are unstressed, with vowel shortening/reduction and their tone neutralised to a mere high or low register. Stress is thus a stressed-root vs unstressed-clitic distinction, not a positional word-stress rule; a further normal vs contrastive stress among full syllables is suspected but left unanalysed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; only a possible 'normal' vs 'contrastive' degree among stressed syllables is mentioned, not consistently recorded.
new_statements.exceptions: Short vowels occur in open syllables only when unstressed; for some clitics (e.g. animal prefix ne) the stressed form could not be elicited; the two informants sometimes disagreed on forms.
new_statements.domain_note: Syllable/clitic level within words and phrases as transcribed in texts and glossary; unstressed status is a property of grammatical proclitics/enclitics, marked in running text (raised dot = high register, unmarked = low register). No statement about phrase-level prominence beyond pauses.
new_statements.identity_note: Li Fang-Kuei's description rests on data collected in 1941 in a village 3-4 miles north of Huishui (惠水, formerly Tingfan) city, Guizhou, from one main informant; the modern reference description (Bo Wenze 1997) is of Then as spoken in Kapu township, Pingtang county. Glottolog files Li 1966/1967/1968 and Bo 1997 all under tenn1245 (no dialect-level codes), so identity with the catalog key holds, but the variety is 'T'en of Huishui, 1941'.

sources.note: p.423: six tones in normally stressed syllables, only two registers (high/low) in unstressed syllables; proclitic/enclitic syllables (prefix/classifier kjaa 35 > kja', animal prefix ne, te' 'one') are unstressed with vocalic reduction; short vowels occur in open syllables only when unstressed. p.424 'STRESS': only stressed vs unstressed syllables are marked; perhaps a normal and a contrastive stress among stressed syllables, not consistently marked.
Nothing on stress; inventory counts from Bo 1997 only.
